chapter: The Jelly Roll Morton records and Minton's Playhouse
title: Club Baron, Clark Monroe's Uptown House and Minton's
summary: Caldwell clarifies the Club Baron became Clark Monroe's Uptown House, which came after Minton's; the building later belonged to Roy Campanella.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: But I mean did that -- see, what was the other place up there, Doc --
Club Baron Monroe and that old club band used to be --
Where?
That old club band -- say about the -- Duke playing the (unintelligible) band? Well, that was the old Club Baron after that place had got -- the fellow that owned it got killed. [Barren Wilkins]
Oh. Well, I mean which came first, that Club Monroe's place or --
No, Club Baron.
Club Band -- but I mean -- yeah, I know Club Band now, but I mean around the '40's, was Minton's going before Clark Clock?

Minton's started. We opened the place, at Cecil Hotel in 1940, and we remained there (unintelligible) I came back from Philadelphia, playing around, came back with the executive board of Philadelphia local 274, and then he had to put a group back in there again. (unintelligible) artists come down. (unintelligible) buddies way back anyway, and then I put a group back in there.
Yeah. I mean so what I really meant was they always talk of Clark Monroe's Uptown House.
Uptown House, right.
Well, you know, as being one of the places where they worked out their bebop thing.
That's right.
Well, I was wondering, did that come before Minton's?
No, it came after Minton's.
Came after Minton's.

Right. Because I had the group at Small's downstairs. Herman had a group upstairs, and Morris had the trio in the bar. And Charlie used to come down there, called me and said, Hap, you coming over to Monroe? I said, sure, I'll go to Monroe. We called him Money

for short. And we'd -- we'd finish our club date at Small's. We'd all go over to Monroe's at 134th and 7th Avenue, just like about walking across the street. And, see, that was Borah (unintelligible) Wilkins. That why it was (unintelligible) named Club Band, but it was Borah Wilkins Club. Then after he got killed -- that was in the early -- late '20's -- then --
Well now, wait a minute. The Club Borah Band is not the same as -- is that the same as Borah Wilkins Club?
Right.
Where Duke played originally?
Right.
I didn't realize that.
(Simultaneous remarks)
So they just dropped one R out of Borah the Band.
Yes, that's right.
I see. Yeah. Is that still going?

No, that place, after Monroe died, they closed it up. But I don't know what they got in there because Campanella that played shortstop -- played catcher with the Brooklyn Dodgers -- he owns that building now, and he got the liquor store and all there, but I don't know, I guess he use that for his vault downstairs because he carry the most top grade of wine, Italian imported wine, French
imported wine, about the best place you can buy it in Harlem.
